enunciado: Na frase "She works at the fire station", o verbo está no presente simples.
Na frase "They are training now", o tempo verbal empregado é o passado simples.
Na frase "He has lived here for ten years", o tempo verbal empregado é o present perfect.
comentario: Has + particípio: começou no passado e continua.

enunciado: O plural de "child", em inglês, é "childs".
Na frase "I will help you tomorrow", o verbo indica uma ação no futuro.
Na frase "The fire was put out by the firefighters", a estrutura está na voz passiva.
O comparativo de superioridade de "big" é "more big".
O superlativo de "good" é "the goodest".
Na frase "If it rains, we will stay home", a oração introduzida por "if" expressa uma condição.
O passado simples do verbo "to go" é "goed".
Na frase "There are many people here", o verbo "to be" concorda com "people" no plural.
Na frase "Don't touch the wires", a estrutura expressa uma ordem ou proibição.
Na frase "She can swim very well", o verbo "can" expressa obrigação.
The verb form "are often seen" (first paragraph) indicates an action that will happen in the future.
comentario: É **presente simples na voz passiva** (are + seen): fato habitual.

enunciado: The verb form "have become" (first paragraph) expresses an action that started in the past and has effects in the present.
The verb form "can make" (first paragraph) expresses ability or possibility.
The modal verb "should", in "should never be completely abandoned", expresses a prohibition imposed by law.
The modal verb "must" (third paragraph) expresses obligation or necessity.
comentario: A good officer must make quick decisions.

enunciado: The modal verb "should" (second paragraph) expresses a recommendation given by lifeguards.
The modal verb "should", in "governments should invest" (fourth paragraph), expresses an ability that governments already have.
The terms "inhaling" and "exhaling" (third paragraph) are verbs that express the idea that the action is happening now.
comentario: Gabarito: ERRADO (apostila). Em "the inhaling and exhaling of CO2", funcionam como **substantivos** (gerúndio nominal), não como presente contínuo.

enunciado: In "Firefighters arrived quickly", the verb is in the present perfect.
comentario: É **simple past** (arrived); present perfect seria "have arrived".

enunciado: In "The team was working when the alarm rang", "was working" is in the past continuous, indicating an action in progress in the past.
In "The team was working when the alarm rang", the verb "rang" is in the present perfect.
The sentence "They have already finished the rescue" indicates an action completed at an unspecified time with relevance to the present.
The sentence "I have seen the fire yesterday" is grammatically correct in standard English.
comentario: Com tempo passado definido (yesterday), usa-se o **simple past**: "I saw the fire yesterday".

enunciado: In "By the time help arrived, the fire had destroyed the house", "had destroyed" is in the past perfect, indicating an action before another past action.
In "The building is going to collapse", the structure "is going to" expresses a future event based on present evidence.
The modal verb "may", in "Smoke may cause breathing problems", expresses certainty.
The modal "must", in "He must be exhausted after the shift", expresses a logical deduction.
The modals "should" and "ought to" can both express advice or recommendation.
In "You mustn't enter the burning building", "mustn't" expresses that it is not necessary to enter.
In "You don't have to wear a uniform today", "don't have to" expresses lack of obligation.
The modal "could", in "Could you help me?", expresses obligation.
In "The victims were rescued by the firefighters", the verb is in the active voice.
The passive form of "The firefighters rescued the victims" is "The victims were rescued by the firefighters".
comentario: Objeto vira sujeito; be no mesmo tempo.

enunciado: In "If I had more time, I would study more", the sentence expresses a hypothetical situation in the present (second conditional).
In "If you heat water to 100 °C, it boils", the zero conditional expresses a general truth.
In "If it had rained, the fire would have been controlled", the sentence refers to a real situation in the future.
The comparative of "dangerous" is "dangerouser".
The comparative of "bad" is "badder".
In "Smoke from large fires can travel thousands of kilometres", the word "large" is an adverb.
In "Swimming near lifeguards is safer", the word "Swimming" functions as a noun (gerund), being the subject of the sentence.
In "They are swimming", the word "swimming" functions as a noun.
comentario: Com auxiliar (are), é **verbo** no presente contínuo.

enunciado: In "a burning building", the word "burning" works as an adjective describing the building.
The past participle of "take" is "took", as in "Measures have been took".
The simple past of "bring" is "brang".
The plural of "woman" is "womans".
In "Each firefighter has his own equipment", the verb "has" agrees with the singular subject "Each firefighter".
The sentence "She don't work on Sundays" is correct in standard English.
The words "much" and "many" are interchangeable, both being used with countable and uncountable nouns.
In "There is little water left", "little" indicates a large quantity of water.
The modal verb "can't", in "That can't be true", expresses a logical conclusion that something is impossible.
The future form "will" can be used for decisions made at the moment of speaking, as in "I'll call an ambulance!".
In "The alarm has been ringing for ten minutes", the present perfect continuous emphasizes the duration of an action that started in the past and continues.
In "He used to work as a lifeguard", the structure "used to" refers to a habit or state in the future.
comentario: "Used to" = hábito ou estado **no passado** que não existe mais.

enunciado: In standard English, adjectives usually come after the nouns they modify, as in "equipment heavy".
comentario: Em inglês, o adjetivo vem **antes**: "heavy equipment".

enunciado: In "Firefighters must be prepared for almost anything", the structure "must be prepared" combines a modal verb with a passive form.
